chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man asked my father about the wars of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the questioner was from our lovers. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him:

God sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with five swords, three of which are unsheathed and will not be sheathed until 'War lays down its burdens', and War will not lay down its burdens until the sun rises from its west, then on that day 'Not will be the faith of a soul which had no faith before or had earned good through its faith'.
Not will be the faith of a soul which had no faith before or had earned good through its faith

And one of them is sheathed (makhfuf) and one is fully sheathed (maghmad); its drawing is for others and its ruling is for us. As for the three unsheathed swords: the first sword is against the polytheists of the Arabs. God Almighty said, 'Fight the polytheists wherever you find them'. These are accepted from them only killing or entering Islam.
Fight the polytheists wherever you find them

And the second sword is against the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah). God Almighty said, 'Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day', the verse. These are accepted from them only the Jizya (tax) or killing.
Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day

And the third sword is a sword against the polytheists of the Ajam (non-Arabs), meaning the Turks, Khazar, and Daylamites. God Almighty said, 'Strike the necks until when you have inflicted defeat upon them'. These are accepted from them only killing or entering Islam, and marriage to them is not permissible for us as long as they are in war.
Strike the necks until when you have inflicted defeat upon them

And as for the sheathed sword (Makhfuf), it is against the People of Revolt (Ahl al-Bagh) and Interpretation. God Almighty said, 'And if two factions among the believers fight, then make peace between them', until His saying, 'Until they return to Allah's command'. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Indeed, among you is one who will fight after me based on Interpretation just as I fought based on Revelation'.
And if two factions among the believers fight, then make peace between them
Until they return to Allah's command

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'Who is he?', and he said, 'He is the Sandal-Mender', meaning the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). And 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: I fought with this banner with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) three times, and this is the fourth. By God, even if they struck us until we reached the palm shoots of Hajjar, we would know that we are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood.

And the conduct (Sira) of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) towards them was like the conduct of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) towards the people of Mecca on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, for he did not enslave their descendants. And he said, 'Whoever closes his door and throws down his weapon or enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe'.

And thus the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said on the day of Basra regarding them, 'Do not enslave their descendants, do not finish off the wounded, do not pursue the fleeing, and whoever closes his door and throws down his weapon is safe'.

And as for the fully sheathed sword (Maghmad), it is the sword of Qisas (retaliation). God Almighty said, 'Life for life', the verse. Its drawing is for the heirs of the slain, and its ruling is for us.

These are the swords with which God sent His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Whoever denies them or denies one of them or something of their conduct and rulings has disbelieved in what God revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَغْيِ: People of Revolt (those who rebel against the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the five types of swords (categories of warfare) described in Shia hadith regarding the Imam's authority?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* categorizes jihad into five 'swords,' linking specific Quranic verses to distinct targets: Arab polytheists, People of the Book, and non-Arab polytheists (unsheathed); the Ahl al-Bagh (sheathed); and Qisas (fully sheathed). It highlights the Imam's central role in adjudicating these categories, particularly noting that the 'sword of interpretation' against the Ahl al-Bagh was prophesied to be wielded by Imam Ali, as indicated by the 'sand-sandal maker' reference. The text concludes that denial of any of these swords or their associated rulings constitutes disbelief in the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad.
